Each figure is A100's dense per-SM tensor rate (whitepaper) x 70 SMs x 1,470 MHz, the sustained clock of an 8 GB card on the 300 W VBIOS, the same configuration as the bandwidth. The unlocked cards' own mma throughput lands just under these (satspace: BF16 201.55, INT8 409.77, TF32 99.82). Through torch, cuBLAS or OpenCL, INT8 measured only 43-48 TOPS in July 2026, against 335-410 TOPS in mma microbenchmarks; that gap is unresolved. llama.cpp issues mma directly, so the higher figure is the bound. No FP8, FP6 or FP4 (sm_80). Sparse rates were never measured on this card, so none are recorded. units.note: A GA100 mining card that becomes a 64 GB inference card through a community unlock (cmpunlocker). The unlock patches the NVIDIA open kernel modules to address the HBM2e already on the card, 4 stacks of 16 GB on a 4096-bit bus, and to lift the compute throttle that left stock cards at 1/32 issue rate. Caveats: only the 8 GB card (PCI 10de:20c2) unlocks to 64 GB; the 10 GB card (10de:2082) reaches 40 GB, and nvidia-smi does not tell them apart. CUDA allocates about 63.4 GiB. Bandwidth depends on the card's VBIOS: 1,769 GB/s is the 300 W image (HBM at 1,728 MHz); the stock 250 W image runs 1,458 MHz for 1,493 GB/s. Both ship under the same ID, and the ceiling takes the faster. The patched driver pins exact versions (610.43.02/.03, 610.57.04, 615.71.09, 615.78.08 as of 2026-10-07), needs Secure Boot off and a cold power cycle, and is Linux-only. ECC is fused off; cmpunlocker reports it enabled since 2026-10-04, but nobody has shown it correcting errors, and one card needed a single-bit HBM page blacklisted by hand. The host link is PCIe Gen1 x4 stock. Gen2 comes from software, x16 from hand-soldering 24 missing capacitors, and Gen3 is unsolved. There is no NVLink. Memory and SM overclocks can corrupt data silently. Passively cooled, on a single EPS 8-pin.

interconnect.note: Intel datasheet 817799: each card has six 53 Gbps SerDes ports. The X2 bridge (99ARXG) joins two cards with six Xe Link connections between them; the X4 bridge (99ARXX) gives each pair of four cards two. The datasheet states no GB/s: whether a connection is one lane or several changes the aggregate about eightfold, so none is recorded. Host link is PCIe 5.0 x16 at 32 GT/s (128 GB/s counted AMD's way; about 63 GB/s per direction after encoding). A separate Xe Link Bridge Card Datasheet (788941) should state the bandwidth and could not be found. The two-card bridge usually ships with a pair of cards and costs about $70 when bought separately. The maintainer has never seen a four-card (X4) bridge for sale, so a four-card rig is not purchasable as far as is known.

host.note: PCIe cards, so the host supplies everything: two x16 slots, ideally PCIe 5.0, spaced for the two-card Xe Link bridge, and a supply with a CEM 5.1 12V-2x6 auxiliary connector per card at up to 300 W each (Intel datasheet 817799). interconnect.note: Cost covers the carrier and the parts it cannot run without, at the post's 2025 prices before VAT, shipping and buying-agent fees. The carrier is about $690 (no AOM-SXMV below 5,000 yuan on Xianyu when the author came to buy, down from about 2,000 yuan earlier) to $900 (a Supermicro refurbished-parts quote, two-unit minimum). On top of that: a case with fans and a 1,400 W power supply (about $300), two JPCIE-to-PCIe cables (about $20 each) and four heatsinks (about $20 each). The high end adds four $50 brackets for the PG199's 36 mm heatsink-hole spacing, which the author avoided by filing the heatsinks by hand. NVLink does not work on these cards, so peers talk over PCIe. The post's cards ran at PCIe 3.0 x16 at best, two GPUs sharing each of the carrier's switches, and slower behind a bifurcated host slot. The host link is therefore PCIe 3.0 x16, not the card's rated 4.0.

host.note: Two host x16 slots feed the carrier, one per switch. The post's Ryzen 9 7950X has 24 CPU lanes, which forced bifurcation and slowed the second pair ("I should have at least 32"). The case supplies the GPUs' power independently of the host. The host is not priced.
